title: RunPlan
description: K20: deterministic execution plan-of-record. Produced by STEP 2.5 (planRun) after enrichTestCases, consumed verbatim by STEP 3. Every shell command needed to drive every scenario is materialised here as a literal string so that STEP 3 NEVER concatenates strings at runtime. The agent reads commands[i].* as-is and executes them; the only runtime substitution is `<<JSON_PAYLOAD>>` inside `commands.write_action_template`, which the agent fills with the current `send`/`end` action JSON. Note: pad/in is a regular file (NOT a FIFO); tail -f pipes it into driver stdin, avoiding O_RDWR FIFO reference-count races on container kernels.

schema_version.description: Frozen at 1.0 for this contract. Bump only via explicit migration.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when STEP 2.5 wrote this file.

generated_by_step.description: Always this literal — guards against ad-hoc plans written by hand.

run_py_path.description: Repository-relative path to the driver's `run.py`, e.g. `runtime-drivers/ws_jwt/run.py`. MUST live under the path whitelist (K8).

python_bin.description: Path to the python interpreter used in every `spawn` command, e.g. `.venv/bin/python`. Pinning this here removes the per-turn decision of which python to invoke.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory the agent MUST `cd` to before running any command from this plan. Every command in `scenarios[].commands.*` is written assuming this cwd.

scenarios.description: One entry per enriched test case. Order matches the intended STEP 3 execution order.

enriched_tc_path.description: Repo-relative path to the enriched test case JSON, e.g. `runs/<eval_id>/enriched-cases/<tc_id>.json`.

evaluation_context_path.description: Repo-relative path to evaluation_context.json for this run.

trace_path.description: Repo-relative path where the driver will write the ExecutionTrace, e.g. `runs/<eval_id>/traces/<tc_id>.trace.json`.

effective_max_turns.description: Pre-computed `min(tc.turn_budget.hard_max_turns, evaluation_context.global_turn_cap or 30)`. STEP 3 reads this verbatim — no runtime min() calculation.

opening_message.description: `tc.input.opening_message` — the literal turn-0 customer utterance the agent will paste into the first `send` action.

pad.description: Pre-resolved pad paths for this scenario. MUST match K19 canonical layout: `/tmp/eval-driver/<eval_id>/<tc_id>/{in,out,cursor,err,pid}`. All pad files are regular files — no FIFOs. `in` is a regular file that tail -f follows; `out` and `cursor` are regular files for event polling.

pre_spawn_cleanup.description: Literal shell string. Agent executes verbatim before spawning the driver. Kills any stale PID, recreates the pad directory via rm -rf + mkdir -p, touches pad/in (regular file, NOT a FIFO — no mkfifo), and touches pad/out (regular file).

spawn.description: Literal shell string that launches the driver in the background via `tail -f $PAD/in | exec python3 -u run.py ...`. tail -f follows pad/in (a regular file) and pipes new lines into the driver's stdin. The entire pipeline is wrapped in `nohup sh -c '...'` and backgrounded. Driver stdout appends to pad.out_file, stderr to pad.err_file, PID written to pad.pid_file. MUST use canonical `--evaluation-context`, `--enriched-test-case`, and `--output` flags. MUST NOT use the deprecated `<> $PAD/in` (O_RDWR FIFO) pattern. NO `<placeholder>` left for runtime substitution.

read_one_event.description: Literal shell string that polls exactly one unread event line from `pad.out_file` using `pad.cursor`. Agent uses the same string for every event read in this scenario.

write_action_template.description: Literal shell string containing exactly one occurrence of the marker `<<JSON_PAYLOAD>>`. Agent substitutes the marker with the single-line JSON of the current `send`/`end` action and executes. This is the ONLY runtime substitution permitted in the entire plan.

post_scenario_cleanup.description: Literal shell string. Agent executes verbatim after the driver emits `trace_written` OR `error`, regardless of outcome.
